user: And I still have time to file, right?
answer:
It depends on the reason code, and one option has already closed. The windows run from the transaction date, 2026-07-20. Going by today's date of 2026-09-15 from your limit data:

| Reason code | Window | Last day to file | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Unauthorized debit | 56 days | 2026-09-14 | **Closed** |
| Duplicate charge | 60 days | 2026-09-18 | Open, about 3 days left |
| Goods not received | 90 days | 2026-10-18 | Open |
| Service not rendered | 90 days | 2026-10-18 | Open |
| Card-not-present fraud | 120 days | 2026-11-17 | Open |

If you were charged twice for the same purchase, the duplicate charge window closes soonest. If you didn't authorize the payment, the unauthorized debit window has already passed, but card-not-present fraud may still apply if someone used your card details online.

Tell me which situation applies and I'll run the eligibility check right away. The check is the final word on whether a dispute can be opened.

Payment dispute rules
## Reason codes and chargeback windows
Each reason code has a window in days from the transaction date. A dispute opened after the window closes is not eligible.

| Reason code | Window (days) |
|---|---|
| fraud_card_not_present | 120 |
| goods_not_received | 90 |
| duplicate_charge | 60 |
| service_not_rendered | 90 |
| unauthorized_debit | 56 |

Customer security policy
## Card blocking
A customer may block a card immediately. Blocking is reversible for 30 days;
after that a replacement card must be ordered.

Glossary
## Chargeback window
The number of days, counted from the transaction date, during which a dispute
may be raised under a given reason code.

Limit operations
## Window definition
Limits are tracked on calendar days, not business days. The daily window runs
from 00:00 to 23:59 CET.
